title: Introduction to Logarithms
objectives: Convert between index form and logarithm form
Evaluate simple logarithms without a calculator
State and use the three laws of logarithms

body.h: A logarithm is a question about a power

body.p: When we write log₁₀ 1000 = 3, we are answering: "10 raised to what power gives 1000?" The answer is 3. So a logarithm is simply an index written the other way round.

body.f: If aˣ = b, then log_a b = x

body.naija: Think of okada fare wey dey double every year: ₦100, ₦200, ₦400, ₦800. If somebody ask "how many years before fare reach ₦800?", you dey ask log₂(800/100) = log₂ 8 = 3 years. Na the same question.

body.h: The three laws you must know cold

body.f: log(MN) = log M + log N
log(M/N) = log M − log N
log(Mⁿ) = n log M

body.p: Evaluate log₁₀ 20 + log₁₀ 5.

list: Use the first law: log₁₀(20 × 5) = log₁₀ 100
10 raised to what power gives 100? The answer is 2
So the value is 2
Writing log M + log N as log(M + N) — it is log(MN)
Forgetting that log 1 = 0 for any base
Trying to take the log of a negative number or zero — it does not exist

title: Electric Fields and Potential
objectives: Define an electric field and state its unit
Calculate field strength around a point charge
Explain electric potential and potential difference

body.p: An electric field is the region around a charged body where its force is felt. Any other charge placed inside that region will either be pulled or pushed. The field is a vector: it has both size and direction, and by convention it points away from a positive charge and towards a negative one.

body.naija: Think of a transformer on your street. You no need to touch am before you know say danger dey there — the closer you go, the more the effect. That "area of influence" na exactly what electric field mean.

body.p: Field strength is the force experienced per unit positive charge placed at that point.

body.f: E = F / Q        (unit: N/C or V/m)

body.p: For a point charge Q, the field at a distance r away is:

body.f: E = kQ / r²      where k = 9.0 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²

body.p: A charge of 2 × 10⁻⁶ C sits in a field and experiences a force of 0.5 N. Find the field strength.
Electric potential at a point is the work done in bringing one coulomb of positive charge from infinity to that point.

body.f: V = W / Q = kQ / r      (unit: volt, V)

body.p: Potential is a scalar — no direction. Potential difference between two points is simply the work done moving one coulomb from one point to the other, and that is exactly what your voltmeter reads.

list: Mixing up field strength (vector, N/C) with potential (scalar, V)
Forgetting to square r in the E = kQ/r² formula
Leaving the charge in microcoulombs instead of converting to coulombs

title: Understanding the Mole
objectives: Define the mole and Avogadro number
Convert between mass, moles and number of particles
Apply the mole to gas volumes at s.t.p.

body.h: The mole is just a counting word

body.p: A dozen means 12. A carton of Peak milk means 24 tins. In the same way, a mole means 6.02 × 10²³ particles. That number is called Avogadro constant, and the particles can be atoms, molecules, ions or electrons — you must always say which.

body.naija: For market, you no dey buy egg one by one — you dey buy crate. Crate na 30 eggs. Chemist too no fit count atom one by one, so dem take mole as their own crate. Just that this crate na 602 followed by 21 zeros.

body.h: The three formulas that carry everything

body.f: number of moles = mass (g) ÷ molar mass (g/mol)
number of particles = moles × 6.02 × 10²³
volume of gas at s.t.p. = moles × 22.4 dm³

body.p: How many moles are in 44 g of carbon dioxide? (C = 12, O = 16)

list: Molar mass of CO₂ = 12 + (16 × 2) = 44 g/mol
Moles = 44 ÷ 44 = 1 mole
So it also contains 6.02 × 10²³ molecules and occupies 22.4 dm³ at s.t.p.
Using atomic mass where molar mass of the whole compound is needed
Forgetting that 22.4 dm³ only applies at s.t.p., not at room temperature
Saying "one mole of oxygen" without stating atoms or molecules
